reading-text-1.label: 阅读 Text 1
reading-text-1.title: 2010 考研英语二 阅读 Text 1

paragraphs.en: The longest bull run in a century of art-market history ended on a dramatic note with a sale of 56 works by Damien Hirst, “Beautiful Inside My Head Forever”, at Sotheby’s in London on September 15th, 2008. All but two pieces sold, fetching more than £70m, a record for a sale by a single artist. It was a last victory. As the auctioneer called out bids, in New York one of the oldest banks on Wall Street, Lehman Brothers, filed for bankruptcy.
paragraphs.zh: 2008 年 9 月 15 日，伦敦苏富比拍卖行拍卖了达米安·赫斯特 (Damien Hirst) 的 56 件作品《永远美丽在我的脑海中》，艺术市场史上最长的牛市以戏剧性的方式结束。除两件作品外，其余作品全部售出，成交价超过 7000 万英镑，创下了单一艺术家的拍卖纪录。这是最后的胜利。当拍卖师发出竞价时，纽约华尔街最古老的银行之一雷曼兄弟公司申请破产。

paragraphs.en: The world art market had already been losing momentum for a while after rising bewilderingly since 2003. At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm— double the figure five years earlier. Since then it may have come down to $50 billion. But the market generates interest far beyond its size because it brings together great wealth, enormous egos, greed, passion and controversy in a way matched by few other industries.
paragraphs.zh: 自 2003 年以来，世界艺术市场在经历了令人眼花缭乱的增长之后，已经有一段时间失去了动力。研究公司 Arts Economics 的创始人克莱尔·麦克安德鲁 (Clare McAndrew) 估计，在 2007 年达到顶峰时，其价值约为 650 亿美元，是五年前这一数字的两倍。从那时起，这一数字可能已降至 500 亿美元。但这个市场产生的兴趣远远超出了它的规模，因为它以其他行业很少能比拟的方式汇集了巨大的财富、巨大的自负、贪婪、激情和争议。

paragraphs.en: In the weeks and months that followed Mr. Hirst’s sale, spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable. In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms. Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in the year to November 2008. Within weeks the world’s two biggest auction houses, Sotheby’s and Christie’s, had to pay out nearly $200m in guarantees to clients who had placed works for sale with them.
paragraphs.zh: 在赫斯特先生出售之后的几周和几个月里，任何形式的支出都变得非常不流行。在艺术界，这意味着收藏家远离画廊和拍卖场。当代艺术品的销售额下降了三分之二，在最过热的领域，截至 2008 年 11 月的一年内下降了近 90%。几周之内，世界上最大的两家拍卖行苏富比和佳士得就不得不向向其出售作品的客户支付近 2 亿美元的担保金。

paragraphs.en: The current downturn in the art market is the worst since the Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989. This time experts reckon that prices are about 40% down on their peak on average, though some have been far more fluctuant. But Edward Dolman, Christie’s chief executive, says: “I’m pretty confident we’re at the bottom.”
paragraphs.zh: 目前艺术品市场的低迷是自 1989 年底日本停止购买印象派画家以来最严重的一次。专家估计，这次价格比峰值平均下跌了 40% 左右，尽管有些价格波动更大。但佳士得首席执行官爱德华·多尔曼 (Edward Dolman) 表示：“我非常有信心我们已经处于谷底。”

paragraphs.en: What makes this slump different from the last, he says, is that there are still buyers in the market. Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack of good work to sell. The three Ds—death, debt and divorce—still deliver works of art to the market. But anyone who does not have to sell is keeping away, waiting for confidence to return.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，这次衰退与上次不同的是，市场上仍然有买家。几乎所有接受本专题报道采访的人都表示，目前最大的问题不是缺乏需求，而是缺乏好作品可卖。三个 D——死亡、债务和离婚——仍然将艺术品推向市场。但任何不需要出售的人都在远离，等待信心恢复。

reading-text-2.label: 阅读 Text 2
reading-text-2.title: 2010 考研英语二 阅读 Text 2

paragraphs.en: I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room—a women’s group that had invited men to join them. Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative, frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch. Toward the end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don’t talk to them. This man quickly nodded in agreement. He gestured toward his wife and said, “She’s the talker in our family.” The room burst into laughter; the man looked puzzled and hurt. “It’s true,” he explained. “When I come home from work, I have nothing to say. If she didn’t keep the conversation going, we’d spend the whole evening in silence.”
paragraphs.zh: 我当时正在弗吉尼亚郊区客厅的一个小型聚会上发表讲话，这是一个邀请男性加入的妇女团体。整个晚上，一名男子特别健谈，经常提出想法和轶事，而他的妻子则默默地坐在他旁边的沙发上。晚上快结束时，我评论说，女性经常抱怨她们的丈夫不和她们说话。这人连忙点头答应。他指着他的妻子说：“她是我们家里最健谈的人。”房间里爆发出一阵笑声。那人看上去既困惑又受伤。 “这是真的，”他解释道。 “当我下班回家时，我无话可说。如果她不继续谈话，我们整个晚上都会保持沉默。”

paragraphs.en: This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in public situations, they often talk less at home. And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage.
paragraphs.zh: 这一集体现了一个讽刺之处：尽管美国男性在公共场合比女性说话更多，但在家里却往往说话更少。这种模式正在对婚姻造成严重破坏。

paragraphs.en: The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s. Sociologist Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she interviewed—but only a few of the men—gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces. Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the United States every year—a virtual epidemic of failed conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 政治学家安德鲁·哈克 (Andrew Hacker) 在 20 世纪 70 年代末观察到了这一模式。社会学家凯瑟琳·科勒·里斯曼（Catherine Kohler Riessman）在她的新书《离婚谈话》中报告说，她采访的大多数女性（但只有少数男性）都将缺乏沟通作为离婚的原因。鉴于目前近 50% 的离婚率，美国每年的离婚率达到数百万起——几乎是失败对话的流行病。

paragraphs.en: In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on tangible inequities such as having given up the chance for a career to accompany a husband to his, or doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements. Instead, they focused on communication: “He doesn’t listen to me.” “He doesn’t talk to me.” I found, as Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost, conversational partners, but few husbands share this expectation of their wives.
paragraphs.zh: 在我自己的研究中，女性对丈夫的抱怨往往不是集中在有形的不平等上，比如放弃了陪伴丈夫的职业机会，或者做的远远超过了她们承担的日常生活支持工作，如清洁、烹饪和社交安排。相反，他们专注于沟通：“他不听我的。” “他不跟我说话。”我发现，正如哈克多年前所观察到的那样，大多数妻子希望她们的丈夫首先成为谈话伙伴，但很少有丈夫对妻子抱有这样的期望。

paragraphs.en: In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at the back of it, wanting to talk.
paragraphs.zh: 简而言之，最能代表当前危机的形象是一个典型的卡通场景：一个男人坐在早餐桌前，面前举着一份报纸，而一个女人则盯着报纸后面，想要说话。

reading-text-3.label: 阅读 Text 3
reading-text-3.title: 2010 考研英语二 阅读 Text 3

paragraphs.en: Over the past decade, many companies had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors—habits—among consumers. These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often in response to a carefully designed set of daily cues. “There are fundamental public health problems, like dirty hands instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can’t figure out how to change people’s habits,” said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. “We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically.”
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的十年里，许多公司已经完善了在消费者中创造自动行为（习惯）的艺术。当顾客几乎不假思索地吃零食或擦拭柜台时，这些习惯帮助公司赚取了数十亿美元，这通常是对一组精心设计的日常提示的反应。伦敦卫生与热带医学院卫生中心主任柯蒂斯博士说：“一些基本的公共卫生问题，比如脏手而不是使用肥皂的习惯，仍然是杀手，只是因为我们不知道如何改变人们的习惯。” “我们想向私营企业学习如何创造自动发生的新行为。”

paragraphs.en: The companies that Dr. Curtis turned to—Procter & Gamble, Colgate-Palmolive and Unilever—had invested hundreds of millions of dollars finding the subtle cues in consumers’ lives that corporations could use to introduce new routines. If you look hard enough, you’ll find that many of the products we use every day—chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins—are results of manufactured habits. A century ago, few people regularly brushed their teeth multiple times a day. Today, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habitually give their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands.
paragraphs.zh: 柯蒂斯博士求助的公司——宝洁公司、高露洁棕榄公司和联合利华公司——已经投资了数亿美元，寻找消费者生活中的微妙线索，企业可以利用这些线索来引入新的生活习惯。如果你仔细观察，你会发现我们每天使用的许多产品——口香糖、皮肤保湿剂、消毒湿巾、空气清新剂、净水器、健康零食、牙齿美白剂、织物柔软剂、维生素——都是人为习惯的结果。一个世纪前，很少有人每天定期刷牙多次。如今，由于精明的广告和公共卫生运动，许多美国人习惯性地每天两次给他们的珍珠白皮肤涂上防蛀牙磨砂膏，通常使用高露洁、佳洁士或其他品牌的产品。

paragraphs.en: A few decades ago, many people didn’t drink water outside of a meal. Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long. Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is now featured in commercials as a breath freshener and teeth cleanser for use after a meal. Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting on makeup. “Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly patterns,” said Carol Berning, a consumer psychologist who recently retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year. “Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers’ lives, and it’s essential to making new products commercially viable.”
paragraphs.zh: 几十年前，许多人饭后不喝水。后来饮料公司开始将遥远的泉水生产装瓶，现在上班族整天不假思索地喝着瓶装水。口香糖曾经主要由青春期男孩购买，现在在广告中被用作餐后使用的口气清新剂和牙齿清洁剂。皮肤保湿霜被宣传为早晨美容仪式的一部分，在梳头和化妆之间使用。 “当我们的产品成为日常或每周模式的一部分时，我们的产品就成功了，”最近从宝洁公司退休的消费者心理学家卡罗尔·伯宁（Carol Berning）说，宝洁公司去年销售了 760 亿美元的汰渍、佳洁士和其他产品。 “养成积极的习惯是改善消费者生活的重要组成部分，对于使新产品具有商业可行性至关重要。”

paragraphs.en: Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising. As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.
paragraphs.zh: 通过实验和观察，伯宁博士等社会科学家了解到，通过无情的广告将某些行为与习惯线索联系起来是有力量的。随着这种新的习惯科学的出现，当这种策略被用来销售有问题的美容霜或不健康食品时，争议就会爆发。

reading-text-4.label: 阅读 Text 4
reading-text-4.title: 2010 考研英语二 阅读 Text 4

paragraphs.en: Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete expression of crucial democratic values, including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race, religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts should represent the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law. The jury is also said to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy. In a direct democracy, citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them.
paragraphs.zh: 许多美国人认为陪审团制度是关键民主价值观的具体体现，其中包括所有符合最低年龄和文化水平的公民都平等有能力担任陪审员的原则；陪审员应从具有代表性的社区中随机选出；任何公民不应因种族、宗教、性别或国籍而被剥夺担任陪审团成员的权利；被告有权接受同侪的审判；判决应该代表社会良心，而不仅仅是法律条文。陪审团也被认为是现存的直接民主而非代议制民主的最佳范例。在直接民主中，公民轮流自治，而不是选举代表来治理。

paragraphs.en: But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals. In some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education, and moral character. Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v. West Virginia, the practice of selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other antidiscrimination laws. The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid- 20th century. Although women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states made women eligible for jury duty. Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list. This practice was justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women through the 1960s.
paragraphs.zh: 但就在 1968 年，陪审团遴选程序与这些民主理想发生了冲突。例如，在一些州，陪审员职责仅限于被认为具有较高智力、教育程度和道德品质的人。尽管美国最高法院早在 1880 年斯特劳德诉西弗吉尼亚州案中就禁止在陪审团选择中存在故意种族歧视，但选择所谓精英或蓝带陪审团的做法为绕过这一法律和其他反歧视法律提供了便捷的方法。直到 20 世纪中叶，该制度也未能定期将女性纳入陪审团。尽管女性于 1898 年首次在犹他州担任州陪审员，但直到 20 世纪 40 年代，大多数州才允许女性担任陪审员。即使在那时，一些州自动免除女性陪审员的职责，除非她们亲自要求将自己的名字列入陪审团名单。这种做法的合理性在于，家庭需要女性，并且在 20 世纪 60 年代，陪审团一直无法代表女性。

paragraphs.en: In 1968, the Congress of the United States passed the Jury Selection and Service Act, ushering in a new era of democratic reforms for the jury. This law abolished special educational requirements for federal jurors and required them to be selected at random from a cross section of the entire community. In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor vs. Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that juries be representative of all parts of the community to the state level. The Taylor decision also declared sex discrimination in jury selection to be unconstitutional and ordered states to use the same procedures for selecting male and female jurors.
paragraphs.zh: 1968年，美国国会通过了《陪审团遴选和服务法案》，开启了陪审团民主改革的新时代。该法律废除了对联邦陪审员的特殊教育要求，并要求他们从整个社区的各个阶层中随机选出。在 1975 年泰勒诉路易斯安那州这一具有里程碑意义的判决中，最高法院将陪审团必须代表社会各阶层的要求扩展到州一级。泰勒裁决还宣布陪审团选择中的性别歧视违宪，并命令各州使用相同的程序来选择男性和女性陪审员。
